selected_result: Theorem 3.4: probabilistic componentwise backward and forward errors for matrix multiplication

bibliographic_source.title: A New Approach to Probabilistic Rounding Error Analysis

paper_locations.anchor: Theorem 3.4 and equations (3.11)-(3.12); the printed j=1:n is disclosed below as an indexing error

task_clarification: For A in R^(m x n), B in R^(n x p), and C=A*B, compute CHat in floating-point arithmetic under the source Model 2.1.

For every lambda>0 and each actual column j=1:p, require a backward representation cHat_j=(A+DeltaA_j)*b_j with |DeltaA_j|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|A| and probability at least Q(lambda,m*n). Also require the full matrix bound |CHat-C|<=gammaTilde_n(lambda)*|A|*|B| with probability at least Q(lambda,m*n*p). The analysis covers all six legal loop orderings of matrix multiplication.

Editorial correction, applied identically to both conditions: printed equation (3.11) says j=1:n although B has p columns. The proof explicitly combines p instances to obtain (3.12), so the intended per-column range is j=1:p. Do not change any other domain, coefficient, event, or conclusion.
scope_constraints: Keep Model 2.1, all rectangular dimensions, both theorem conclusions, their separate probability guarantees, componentwise inequalities, and exact Q and gammaTilde factors.
A candidate giving only the matrix forward bound, or only a square-matrix specialization, is incomplete.
Do not assume the backward perturbations or forward-error event in the execution model.
